title: Fibre restriction of the proper-support pullback map
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring. Let
$$X'\xrightarrow{a}X,\; f'\downarrow,\; f\downarrow,\; Y'\xrightarrow{b}Y$$
be a Cartesian square of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-fibre-product], with $f$ separated and locally of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $F$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Use direct image and constant-coefficient inverse image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Suppose $G\subseteq f_*F$ and $H\subseteq f'_*a^{-1}F$ are subsheaves with the following section descriptions. For every etale $U\to Y$, $G(U)$ consists of the sections of $F(X\times_YU)$ whose closed support is proper over $U$; for every etale $V\to Y'$, $H(V)$ consists of the sections of $(a^{-1}F)(X'\times_{Y'}V)$ whose closed support is proper over $V$. Here support is the locus of nonzero geometric germs [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and a closed subset is proper over its base if its reduced induced closed subscheme is proper [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base].
Let $\alpha:G\to b_*H$ be the section-pullback morphism of [lem-cbc-proper-support-pullback-section-map], and let $\beta:b^{-1}G\to H$ be its adjunct. For a geometric point $\bar y':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y'$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], put $\bar y=b\bar y'$. Write $\rho_G$ and $\rho_H$ for the restriction isomorphisms of [lem-cbc-proper-support-geometric-stalk] from $G_{\bar y}$ and $H_{\bar y'}$ to the modules of fibre sections whose closed support is proper over $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Let
$$c:(b^{-1}G)_{\bar y'}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{\bar y}$$
be the germ-compatible inverse-image stalk identification [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. The square is Cartesian, so it identifies $X'_{\bar y'}$ with $X_{\bar y}$; inverse-image composition identifies their coefficient sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]. Under these identifications the following equality of maps to the same module of properly supported fibre sections holds:
$$\rho_H\circ\beta_{\bar y'}=\rho_G\circ c.$$
More explicitly, for every pointed etale neighbourhood $(U,\bar u)$ of $\bar y$ and $s\in G(U)$, both sides send the germ of the unit pullback of $s$ on $U\times_YY'$ to the restriction of $s$ along $X_{\bar y}\to X\times_YU$.

proof.text: Use properSupport_geometricStalk twice, for f at y' composed with b and for f' at y'. Base-change stability supplies the separated and locally finite type instances for f'. Retain the normalized restriction transformations, their proper-support submodules, and their inclusion equations.

Paste the Cartesian square with the pullback defining the fibre over y'. Its universal property gives the canonical isomorphism d from the new fibre to the original fibre, with both projection equations. Compose the ModuleCat inverse-image composition isomorphisms to identify i'^* a^* F with d^* i^* F. Evaluation on the terminal etale object and inverse pullback along d give the ambient section isomorphism k.

The inverse-image unit and geometric-germ comparison identify zero germs after pullback along an isomorphism with the original zero germs. Using the geometric characterization of closed support, sheaf isomorphisms preserve supports and pullback along d carries the support to its inverse image. Properness over Spec Omega is invariant under this isomorphism by proper_iso_image. Thus k carries the H-fibre proper-support submodule isomorphically to the G-fibre proper-support submodule. Restrict k to obtain kappa and its inclusion equation.

Apply upperStarComp_hom_app_unit_app directly with ModuleCat coefficients. Naturality of the units gives the formula for two successive unit pullbacks followed by restriction. Compare the two resulting pointed lifts into the same pullback: their first projections agree by the marked-point and canonical fibre-isomorphism equations, and their second projections agree because both maps lie over the fibre. This proves that k sends the restriction of properSupportUnitPullback(s) to the restriction of s, for every ambient representative.

Compute the ModuleCat unit-germ identity directly using the point comap comparison and uniqueness of left adjoints. The adjunct unit equation then identifies the stalk image of the inverse pullback germ with the germ of alpha(s). Cancel the proper-support submodule inclusion, precompose with the inverse source stalk comparison, and test on every pointed neighbourhood. Germ naturality, the two normalized restriction equations, the assumed section equation for alpha, and the representative identity from the preceding step give equal underlying sections. The colimit universal property of the geometric stalk and monicity of the submodule inclusion give the required equality.
